findings.issue_text: .panel's right-alignment relies on margin-left: auto, which legacy flexbox engines targeted by the flexbox() mixin (old Android WebView, IE10) don't support, causing the panel to not render flush-right

No shrink protection after removing floats: long unbroken topic titles with white-space:nowrap can push .panel (search input, user buttons) off the right edge of the viewport, a regression from the float layout

.small-action forced to display: flex makes every child a row item, not just avatar and desc; posts with additional body content children will be laid out horizontally and vertically centered, breaking those layouts
Vertical spacing stripped from .small-action-desc with no replacement: removal of vertical padding/margins leaves text flush against the row's border-top, risking a cramped/clipped appearance
align-items() mixin omits -moz-box-align while flexbox() emits display: -moz-box, so old Firefox builds get no vertical centering, and it emits a nonexistent -ms-align-items property

The removed .title rule and reliance on order/margin-left: auto in topic.scss/header.scss only work inside flex containers; if the parent .extra-info-wrapper's parent (topic title area) isn't a flex container, the @include order(2) badge/title ordering silently no-ops (P3 layout-correctness concern, confidence 25-50)

.small-action-desc no longer fills the remaining row width as a shrink-to-fit flex item; missing flex: 1 causes right-floated post info (e.g. .post-info.post-date) to land at the box's right edge instead of the row's right edge
.contents flex row cannot wrap (flex-wrap: nowrap default), so a large logo and panel will shrink or overflow the header instead of stacking like the old float layout, breaking narrow viewports

flexbox() mixin emits 2009-spec -webkit-box/-moz-box prefixes without the properties needed for the new layout (e.g. margin-left: auto doesn't right-align .panel in the old box model, needs -webkit-box-pack: end); also -ms-align-items is a nonexistent property (dead code)

order: 2 on .extra-info-wrapper may be a silent no-op if it is not a direct child of the .contents flex container (e.g. if rendered under .wrap); if it is inside .contents, its vertical alignment under align-items: center and removed .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top compensation need template verification

Floats on direct children of the new flex containers (.contents, .small-action) are silently ignored, so plugin/theme components injecting floated elements into these containers will mislayout with no build-time error, and themes overriding .small-action-desc padding-left: 4em may double-apply or mis-indent

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .panel's right-alignment relies on margin-left: auto, which legacy flexbox engines targeted by the flexbox() mixin (old Android WebView, IE10) don't support, causing the panel to not render flush-right

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `.panel { float: right; }` and replaces it with `margin-left: auto;` inside a new flex container (`.contents { @include flexbox(); }`). Whether `margin-left: auto` works to push a flex item to the right depends on flexbox implementation details in older engines (which the `flexbox()` mixin is explicitly trying to target via `-webkit-box`, `-moz-box`, `-ms-flexbox`, etc.). The finding is a specific, diff-grounded compatibility concern, but the diff alone cannot verify that those legacy engines actually fail to honor auto margins in this setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No shrink protection after removing floats: long unbroken topic titles with white-space:nowrap can push .panel (search input, user buttons) off the right edge of the viewport, a regression from the float layout

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed from a float-based layout to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and `.panel` no longer floats right, instead relying on `margin-left: auto` and flex `order(3)`. With this flex layout, there is no explicit shrink/overflow handling for the title element (the `.title { float: left; }` rule is removed entirely, and no `min-width: 0`, `flex`, or wrapping/overflow rules are added). In flexbox, long unbreakable content in the left item can prevent shrinking and can push the right-aligned item off-screen, so the reported regression is consistent with what this diff introduces, even though the specific `white-space: nowrap` setting is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action forced to display: flex makes every child a row item, not just avatar and desc; posts with additional body content children will be laid out horizontally and vertically centered, breaking those layouts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.small-action` to `display: flex` via `@include flexbox()` and vertically centers all its direct children with `@include align-items(center)`. This is a broad structural layout change: any direct child of `.small-action` becomes a flex item and will participate in the row layout, not just `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc`. The specific claim that there are “posts with additional body content children” that will definitely break cannot be verified from the diff alone (no markup shown), but the underlying review concern about unintended effects on other children is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Vertical spacing stripped from .small-action-desc with no replacement: removal of vertical padding/margins leaves text flush against the row's border-top, risking a cramped/clipped appearance

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove vertical spacing in `.small-action-desc` (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` -> `padding: 0 1.5%;`) and also zeros out inner paragraph margins (`p { margin: 5px 0; }` -> `margin: 0;`), so the finding is grounded in the change. Whether this actually makes the text cramped/clipped against the row border can’t be confirmed from the diff alone (it may be mitigated by the new flex alignment on `.small-action` and existing padding on `.topic-avatar`), so it’s more of a potential UI regression concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items() mixin omits -moz-box-align while flexbox() emits display: -moz-box, so old Firefox builds get no vertical centering, and it emits a nonexistent -ms-align-items property

The removed .title rule and reliance on order/margin-left: auto in topic.scss/header.scss only work inside flex containers; if the parent .extra-info-wrapper's parent (topic title area) isn't a flex container, the @include order(2) badge/title ordering silently no-ops (P3 layout-correctness concern, confidence 25-50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds flex-specific properties (@include order(2) in topic.scss .extra-info-wrapper, and margin-left:auto/@include order(3) in header.scss .panel). These only have effect when the element is a flex item (i.e., its parent is a flex container). The diff does make header.scss .contents a flex container (@include flexbox()), so that part is consistent, but for topic.scss the parent flex context for .extra-info-wrapper is not shown in this diff—so the new order(2) may be a no-op unless another (unchanged) rule makes its parent display:flex. This is a real, diff-grounded concern but not a verifiable defect from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action-desc no longer fills the remaining row width as a shrink-to-fit flex item; missing flex: 1 causes right-floated post info (e.g. .post-info.post-date) to land at the box's right edge instead of the row's right edge

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) but does not add any flex-grow to `.small-action-desc` (no `flex: 1` / `@include flex(1)` etc.). As a result, `.small-action-desc` will size to its contents by default in flex layout, which could change how remaining horizontal space is distributed and potentially affect alignment of other siblings. However, the specific claim about a right-floated `.post-info.post-date` ending up in the wrong place cannot be verified from this diff because `.post-info` styles/markup are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .contents flex row cannot wrap (flex-wrap: nowrap default), so a large logo and panel will shrink or overflow the header instead of stacking like the old float layout, breaking narrow viewports

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed from a block containing floated children to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) with no `flex-wrap` specified, so it defaults to `nowrap`. Previously, `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }` could naturally drop/stack when space was constrained; now flex items will stay on one line and instead shrink or overflow depending on their intrinsic/min widths. This makes the finding (no wrapping leading to potential narrow-viewport breakage) grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order: 2 on .extra-info-wrapper may be a silent no-op if it is not a direct child of the .contents flex container (e.g. if rendered under .wrap); if it is inside .contents, its vertical alignment under align-items: center and removed .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top compensation need template verification

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss`, but the diff does not show `.extra-info-wrapper` being a flex item (i.e., no parent `display: flex` is shown for its container). Since `order` only affects direct children of a flex container, this could be a silent no-op depending on the HTML structure, which cannot be verified from this diff alone. The note about alignment/margin-top changes is also contingent on template/layout, so it’s a valid, specific review concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Floats on direct children of the new flex containers (.contents, .small-action) are silently ignored, so plugin/theme components injecting floated elements into these containers will mislayout with no build-time error, and themes overriding .small-action-desc padding-left: 4em may double-apply or mis-indent

adjudication.rationale: The diff converts `.contents` (header.scss) and `.small-action` (topic-post.scss) into flex containers via `@include flexbox()` / `@include align-items(...)`. In flex formatting context, floated direct children no longer affect layout, so any third-party/plugin/theme code that injects elements relying on `float: left/right` inside these containers could mislayout without any compile-time signal. Additionally, `.small-action-desc` padding changes from a fixed left offset (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;`) to `padding: 0 1.5%`, which can break theme overrides that assumed the old left padding. This is a compatibility/extension-surface concern introduced by the change rather than a directly provable core defect in the shown selectors (the diff itself removes the built-in floats on `.title`/`.panel`).
